clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old man presented on March 26 with upper respiratory tract infection symptoms and mild interstitial pneumonia. On April 24, neurological examination revealed hypophonia, ptosis on sustained upward gaze, slight diplopia, and proximal lower limb weakness (4/5 MRC) with normal reflexes. Repetitive nerve stimulation performed the same day showed a 15% decrement in the right nasalis muscle amplitude at 5 Hz stimulation, consistent with a neuromuscular transmission defect. Serological tests for acetylcholine receptor, MUSK, and ryanodin receptor antibodies were negative, and anti-LRP4 antibody testing was ordered but results were not documented. Clinical course, treatment initiation, and response were not documented.
